7. In its Affidavit-in-Opposition, the Respondent No.4 Bangladesh Railway has stated that Bangladesh Railway has exclusive possession and title over the case land since 1882 when it was acquired by the Bangladesh Railway. It has been further stated that the so called Nawab or his descendants were never owners of the land. In Title Suit No. 161 of 1991 Bangladesh Railway was not a party and that it was not bound by the alleged compromise decree. The land was acquired for Bangladesh Railway in 1882 and since then it is railway land and Rajuk has no authority to deal with such land. It has been further stated that the land of C.S. Khatian No. 16868, plot no. 186, Sheet No. 22, Ward No. 3 area 287 was acquired for Railway by declaration No. 342 and the said acquisition was notified in Calcutta Gazette on 6.9.1882 at page no. 774 Part 1. It has been further stated that the case land belonged to Bangladesh Railway. The question of having any building and shopping complex and/or a 5 Star Hotel on the same does not arise at all and the Writ Petitioner has filed the instant Writ Petition to grab, the railway land and as such the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 9. In an Affidavit-in-reply against the Affidavit-in-Opposition of the Respondent No. 1 the petitioner has reiterated that the case land was owned and possessed by Khawza Nawab Yousuf Jan and it subsequently devolved to the vendor Syed Jamil Hasan from whom the Petitioner purchased the same and obtained possession through the process of the court and that the land or part of it was never within the boundary of Osmany Uddyan. It is further asserted that the judgment and decree dated 7.7.1993 and 10.7.1993 respectively passed in Title Suit No. 139 of 1993(Title Suit No. 161 of 1991 of the First court of Dhaka) by the Subordinate Judge, Second court, Dhaka was lawful and contested and never a collusive one. It is further stated that the land was exclusively owned and possessed by the Petitioner and was never in the possession of the Public Works Department or Dhaka City Corporation and the said Public Works Department or Dhaka City Corporation have nothing to do with the same. It is further stated that the Petitioner deposited an amount of 1,00,000/- by Pay Order as registration fees pursuant to which the Project was registered with the said Department and approval of the Project was given by the Government after compliance of all formalities according to the relevant laws and that Annexure J to the Writ Petition for giving approval and clearance by Rajuk for using the case land by the Petitioner on priority basis was rightly Vs. Gone of Bangladesh, Ors I 613LT(HCD) 2008 issued and cancellation of the same by the impugned Memo Annexure K has been done without any show cause notice is arbitrary and without lawful authority. It is further stated that the Criminal Case filed by Rajuk was done with malafide and ulterior motive for harassing the Petitioner and that till today no police report in this regard has been filed. It has been further stated that the question involved in this Writ Petition is whether the impugned Memo has been issued lawfully and not the Petitioner title to the land in question and in the facts and circumstance of the case the impugned Memo is liable to be declared illegal and issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
